top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a new measurement architecture, not just a tighter number: the magic-wavelength condition cancels the light shifts so thousands of neutral atoms are interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts, which differs in kind from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion control. It is independently reproduced at the 10^-18 level (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) and already used for millimetre-scale redshift and constraints on constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation is clean, with the lineage and omitted-contributor reservations stated but not decisive. No award would withhold a mature, verified achievement.
